title: commit-utilization-scenario-matrix
content:
Sheet: Commit Utilization Scenario Matrix (v2)
Owner: Priya Chakrabarti  —  Product: Dedicated capacity pricing, reserved GPU pools, commit modeling
Purpose: Provide scenario-based cost modeling for reserved GPU pools, show break-even points vs burst/on-demand, and produce concrete commit tier recommendations. This is a working spreadsheet and design doc merged into one.

ASSUMPTIONS (editable cells)
- Token throughput conversion: 1 GPU-hour ~= 45M tokens (conservative for mixed batching; depends on model family)
- On-demand (burst) cost per GPU-hour: $6.50 (NVIDIA A10x equivalent)
- Reserved base cost per GPU-hour (no commit): N/A
- Commit tier discounts (monthly equivalent): Tier A 20% (small commit), Tier B 35% (medium commit), Tier C 50% (enterprise commit) — applied to on-demand baseline to compute reserved price
- Idle reservation overhead: assume 10% of reserved cost wasted if utilization < 60% due to heat and baseline services
- Effective $/1M tokens computed using token conversion above

MAIN SCENARIO TABLE
Columns: Scenario | GPU Type | GPUs Reserved | Avg Utilization % | Peak Burst Hrs/mo | Reserved Cost/mo ($) | Burst Cost/mo ($) | Effective $/GPU-hr | Effective $/1M tokens | Notes

Rows:
1) Baseline (conservative) | A10x | 40 | 55% | 150 | 40 * 24 * 30 * $6.50 * (1 - 0.20) = $157,248 | Burst (on-demand) 200 hrs * $6.50 = $1,300 | Reserved effective $/GPU-hr = $157,248 / (40*24*30*0.55) = $9.48 | $9.48 / 45 = $0.21 per 1M tokens | Assumes Tier A commit (20% discount); utilization below 60% -> idle waste applies.

2) Baseline (target) | A10x | 40 | 75% | 80 | Reserved cost = $157,248 (same commit) | Burst 80 * $6.50 = $520 | $157,248 / (40*24*30*0.75) = $6.95 | $6.95 / 45 = $0.154 per 1M tokens | Recommended utilization target for economic viability with Tier A.

3) Aggressive-scale | A100-80GB | 16 | 85% | 40 | Reserved cost (Tier B: 35%) = 16*24*30*$12.00*(1-0.35) = $94,080 | Burst 40*$12 = $480 | Effective $/GPU-hr = $94,080 / (16*24*30*0.85) = $8.12 | $8.12 / 45 = $0.18 per 1M tokens | Higher per-hour base, but better utilization and higher throughput per GPU.

4) Enterprise-commit | A100-80GB | 64 | 65% | 300 | Reserved cost (Tier C: 50%) = 64*24*30*$12.00*(1-0.50) = $165,888 | Burst 300*$12 = $3,600 | Effective $/GPU-hr = $165,888 / (64*24*30*0.65) = $5.97 | $5.97 / 45 = $0.133 per 1M tokens | Deep discount requires high absolute commit; risk if sustained utilization drops.

SENSITIVITY / BREAK-EVEN ANALYSIS (quick checks)
- Break-even utilization vs on-demand for a given discount: Solve ReservedEffectiveCostPerGPUhr(util) = OnDemand*1.0
  Example (Tier A: 20% discount -> reserved nominal price per hr = 0.8 * onDemandPrice). Break-even util considering idle waste: util_break = (0.8)/(1 + idle_overhead) -> numeric approx = 0.8 / 1.1 = 0.727 -> 72.7%
- Table: Discount | Idle overhead | Break-even util
  20% | 10% | 72.7%
  35% | 10% | 54.5%
  50% | 10% | 36.4%

IMPLIED RULES FOR COMMITS (draft recommendations)
- Small commits (monthly <= $100k): prefer Tier A, require utilization target >= 75% or automated scale-to-zero for unused pods to avoid waste.
- Medium commits ($100k-$500k): Tier B preferable; aim for 60-80% utilization with guaranteed pooled bursting region. Add on-call capacity to manage noisier workloads.
- Enterprise commits (>$500k): Tier C recommended; requires strict SLOs for customers and a cross-product chargeback to maintain utilization > 50%. Add rolling reallocation rules to shift low-util workloads to cheaper regions.

OPERATIONAL LEVERS (for product/ops to implement)
- Autoscaler policy: prefer keeping a hot baseline of pooled workers and allow rapid cold-start only for < 5% of capacity to reduce idle waste.
- Prefix and KV caching: increase cache hit target from 25% to 45% for chat workloads to reduce token count per inference and improve effective utilization.
- Scheduling: collocate latency-sensitive workloads on smaller GPU types; batchable workloads on high-memory GPUs.
- Commit windows: quarterly review with rolling 30-day lookback for rebalancing reserved GPU allocation.

RECOMMENDED NEXT STEPS (actionable)
1) Run a 90-day canary: 40-GPU A10x Tier A commit w/ enforced autoscaler rules and daily utilization reporting. Owner: Priya. Deliverable: daily utilization dashboard + weekly cost delta.
2) Build a 'Commit Planner' UI widget in Console that shows break-even utilization and suggested commit tier based on last 30d traffic. Linked artifact: jira:INF-4821.
3) Add model-family-specific tokens-per-GPU-hour estimates to the spreadsheet (open task for Applied ML). Responsible: Marina López.
4) Draft customer-facing commit tiers doc and sample contract language for Finance/Legal review. Owner: Ethan Cole.

NOTES / OPEN QUESTIONS
- Token-per-GPU-hour is model and batch-size dependent. Current 45M token assumption is conservative; we should instrument and publish per-model profiles.
- How to treat multi-tenant noisy neighbors: should we add a 5% buffer by default?
- Should we offer dynamic commit reallocation (credits) if usage falls consistently below target across 2 consecutive months?

CELL EXTRACTS (for fast copying into product dashboard)
- commit_tier_a_discount = 0.20
- commit_tier_b_discount = 0.35
- commit_tier_c_discount = 0.50
- on_demand_a10x = 6.50
- on_demand_a100 = 12.00
- token_per_gpu_hour = 45_000_000

HISTORY / EDIT LOG
- 2025-11-03: initial draft (Priya)
- 2025-12-14: added Aggressive-scale scenario and Tier B math (Ethan)
- 2026-01-21: updated A100 pricing assumptions and added break-even table (Marina)
- 2026-02-28: in-review edits: added next steps and action owners (Priya)

TO-DO (short)
- [ ] Instrument per-model throughput (APPLIED-ML)
- [ ] Hook Console commit-suggestion widget to this sheet
- [ ] Legal review for sample contract addendum

End of sheet.
